utterances.text: Would you draw it in, please, and place a letter "J" on that spot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got a pencil.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan will supply you with one, I see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the purposes of the record, the witness has placed a "J" on the spot where she was sitting during this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you first noticed Mr. Zigic, can you indicate the location where you first saw him and mark it with letter "Z", please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was moving along this way here, going in the direction of the "white house." He was walking around. He wasn't staying put at one place. But I could clearly see the "white house." Nothing obstructed my view. He was walking around this area here between the pista and the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Witness J has indicated, has marked the location where Mr. Zigic was walking with letter "Z".

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were there any people on the pista at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had been pushed into the rooms where they were staying. People didn't stay on the pista all the time. Sometimes they would be taken out on the pista, sometimes they were elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness J, are you familiar with the fact that people from the pista used to sleep in the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes they would when the guard told them so. Sometimes they would sleep under the radiators or on the floor, but only from time to time, occasionally, as far as I could see. I don't know what would happen after I'd been taken to my sleeping quarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you now indicate the spot where Mr. Meakic was staying at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was walking around the area in front of the building, on the pista. He moved about and he could clearly see it. He was working along this area here, towards the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness J, could you mark it with letter "M", please?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the letter "M" indicates the area where Mr. Meakic was, rather the way along which he moved during this particular incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And finally, what about Mr. Kvocka? Where was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there as well. As far as I could see, he was moving along the same route, from the administration building to the "white house" and back. He was also moving along that area behind the restaurant, on the side of the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you please indicate it with a line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was also walking in the area which was to my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the area with letter "K".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness has indicated the path which was taken by Mr. Kvocka at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who did Zigic talk to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He talked to a guard who happened to be there. He was yelling at him. He wanted the people that he had mentioned to be brought to him. He had named them by their names and surnames, and he wanted to know where they were. He didn't know. It is on the basis of that that I came to my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I would like to know how long this yelling of Mr. Zigic lasted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you how long it lasted, but -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Five, ten minutes, one hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a watch. I didn't pay attention to the time. For quite awhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that immediately after that, you went to the toilet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very shortly after that I went to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How long? Could you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you came out, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went back to the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: To the same spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sat down on a chair.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where you had been sitting before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What could you observe at that point? Could you see Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I could see him in front of the "white house." He had somewhat changed his spot. He was standing in front of the "white house".

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What about Mr. Meakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I no longer saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see him after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you, at any point in time, see Mr. Zigic and Meakic talk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What about Mr. Kvocka and Mr. Zigic, did they talk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was it customary, Witness J, for the commander and his deputy to walk around together at the same time, as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would occasionally happen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see any individuals being taken to the "white house" after you had come out of the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were quite visible. Asaf Kapetanovic is no longer alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to the orders. Yesterday and today you spoke about Mr. Kvocka issuing orders to the guards regarding their daily deployments. You said that he would indicate to them their duty post.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Kvocka kill anyone, beat up anyone, verbally abuse anyone, or torture anyone in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness J, did you at any point in time see Mr. Kvocka issue any order to any member of the security personnel to kill anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: To beat up anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: To torture anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness J, after you'd left this unfortunate camp, you were quite active in public regarding the topics concerning the camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you often give statements? Did you take part in various debates, conferences, send messages via e-mail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your profession, your background, and what you have been through, could you tell us whether during those conferences you were telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Always the truth and only the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the title (redacted) ring a bell? Does it tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. What do you mean by "committee"? Would you repeat the question for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will do that. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never heard of such a committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So it means that you were never a member of such a committee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness J, in June 1993, that is, some ten months after the closing down of the unfortunate camp, did you take part in the work of the

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You took an active part in that conference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess you could call it an active part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you make any statements during that conference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did take the floor at one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like the assistance of the usher, please. Could the witness please be given -- this is a copy for the Prosecutor. For the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I please assign the numbers to all those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was following the practice that has been established, that is that, after the examination of the witness, the two documents will be tendered into evidence, including the photograph on which Witness J made certain indications, but only after the cross-examination has been completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Simic, but I think that the document should be marked for evidence right away because later on we will be able to identify the document that you wish to tender. You already have one document, one photograph. Let us make things clear. Madam Registrar, what is going to be the number of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph, D30/1. And for this document, can I have a copy of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for this document that we have now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the English version is D31/1A, for the B/C/S is D31/1B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Now the documents have been marked for identification, and you can refer to them by their respective numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As well, I would like to remind you that we need five copies of all these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will get them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness J, it was a rather significant international event. Is it true that, during that conference, you stated that you had had to work in the camp canteen for 14 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember that particular bit. I gave so many interviews to the TV and other media, but this is -- this comes from the France press. I don't know what exactly you're talking about. I really gave a number of interviews, and, you know, the journalists sometimes --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness -- yes, yes. You made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness J, you have a document in front of you containing the news which were broadcast by all major news agencies. The source in question here is the France press. They quoted your statement, the statement that you made during the world conference that I referred to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: During that conference, according to the quotations made by France press journalists, it seems that you and three other participants at that conference introduced yourself as the Committee of Bosnian Detention Survivors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. We introduced ourselves as women from Bosnia-Herzegovina. I don't know how they quoted us, but during that conference we were representing a non-governmental organisation called "Women of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Witness J, on the basis of a statement that you made during such an important conference, all news agencies broadcast the news that 3.800 people, including women, men, and children, died in the camp of Omarska during the period of time of two months. 3.800 people, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I'm very cautious when it comes to statistics. I'm really reluctant to give any statistical data.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you state this during the conference in question or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. Again, as I told you, I'm always very cautious when it comes to numbers. I did talk about the events that took place there, and I abide by that statement, and I did talk about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness J. A month ago, maybe a month and a half, the media broadcast the news on a judgement rendered by an American court that was acting pursuant to a compensation request made by women of Bosnia against Radovan Karadzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I should like to know whether you have given any statement concerning that event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. A press conference was held in the United States, and I made a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the United States at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Are you one of the individuals that have submitted a compensation claim against Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Our claim was submitted in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This brings me to my last question. Witness J, do you know somebody called Ranko Saric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That completes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Krstan Simic. Mr. Fila is next. Your witness, Mr. Fila. Please begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Witness J, you have your name, of course, but I don't want to address you by your name. I am Toma Fila, attorney, and I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Krkan with my colleague. I'm going to ask you some questions. First of all, could you explain to the Trial Chamber, when you explained the command structure of the camp, you said that the commander of the camp would deploy the shifts, and then you said that the deputies did the same, and then you said that the shift leaders did this. You said how Meakic did this, how the deputies did this. Would you now tell me how Krkan did this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, there's no problem there. I will tell you. I have already said that the guards would come to work in groups. I don't know how many of them there were exactly. I don't want to quote figures. I always remember figures badly. They would then report to the room Krkan was in. Krkan would receive them. I gained the impression that they were all doing this, that they all did this. That it wasn't only the job of the commander or Deputy Commander to do this, that everybody did this: the shift leaders, the commanders, and the commander deputies. That was my impression. They could all deploy these guards, and that the guards had to report to them when coming on duty and the others when they went home. I don't know if I was clear in my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Ah, now I understand, yes. In answering some questions put to you today, you said that you in fact saw the first shift in the morning at 7 a.m., and that, as far as I understood, you didn't see the afternoon shift.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes I would see the afternoon shift, depending on what I was doing. When I was in the restaurant, if I was in the restaurant I could see everything because, as I said, there was glass. The walls were glass and the partitions were glass. So if I was there, I could see; but if I was scrubbing floors or doing something anywhere else, then I would not have occasion to see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said that the shift leaders were in the offices when this happened. One shift would leave, and he would receive the next shift coming on duty. Was that right? Shall we wait for the translation for a little bit, please. Right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krkan would sometimes be downstairs. Sometimes he would go downstairs. Sometimes they would go up to the office. There weren't any strict rules and regulations with respect to that, so I don't -- I'm not always able to say the same thing. It depended.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So they did not come together; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can you tell me where the taps were by the garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You mean by the garage? I don't remember ever being allowed to go there or being taken there at all. I really don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You went on to speak about the following, that is to say, you said the women were put up in two rooms on the upper storey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm not asking you any trick questions; I'm putting straightforward questions to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know. I'm not afraid of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm interested in knowing whether in the "white house," apart from the individual -- the female individuals you mentioned, was there a room or a dormitory for women? Were there several women who were put up there just as you were put up in the building you were put up in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the "white house," I said that there was only one woman accommodated in the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. The rooms you spoke about where you were accommodated, where you stayed during the night -- let me remind you, where you saw the blood and so on -- did interrogations take place in those rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did they take place only in those rooms, or in other rooms as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they took place in other rooms as well. I always slept in one and the same room, always in the same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And what about the other women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other women would be in the room next to mine, in the next-door room.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you show us on the model -- and I have a third question for you. Listen to my questions first and get up afterwards -- so the rooms that -- the room that you were in, that the other women were in, and the room in which the incident with Krkan and the captain took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness stand and indicate these positions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Given the confidentiality measures, I think there are two ways to do this. One, we have to go into closed session so that she can move, or, alternatively, we could have the top half put on the ELMO and she could point to it, because it does come apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, both variants are agreeable. You can decide, the witness maybe decide perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could we place the administration building on the ELMO? I don't know whether that is feasible or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: First of all, indicate, please, the room that you slept in, then the room that your colleagues slept in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the room I slept in.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the other women slept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but perhaps we ought to quote numbers. There are numbers, whereas if we read the transcript, it says "here," or "this room there" and so on. So could you read out the numbers, although they are upside down on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That's better. Now we can see the numbers properly. Would you do it again, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Give us the number, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I have to take up my glasses. It is B4. I was in room B4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there's something wrong again. Witness, take your time to orient yourself. I think Mr. Keegan was going to say something to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think it's the orientation part, because she's testified about left and right and that's her focus. I think either it has to be the way it was or we have to explain to her where the entrance from the stairway was and that would orient her, because we've completely turned it around on her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think there's a problem there. We all saw the model being turned round, and we saw that the witness was not wearing her glasses. Now, Mr. Fila, ask your question again. Start again, please, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Well, I apologise for turning the model around, that's our fault, but let's deal with this matter simply. Give us the number of the room you were in and indicate it to us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: At night I was in room B4.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. As I don't want to use any tricks, it was not like that. So let's ask the witness to take a look one more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think if we could agree and advise the witness that the entrance from the stairway would be where B8 is indicated. So she has to think of herself coming up the stairway and coming into that hallway from B8.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That misled me. That led me astray. I apologise. I was looking at the entrance here. I was looking at it from the opposite side. Had you told me where the entrance was, I would have been able to orient myself straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The entrance is where you're pointing to now. The tip of your pointer is at the entrance. Yes. That's right. Now show us where you were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I cannot orient myself in space very well, find my bearings, but I was in B10. I have this problem of lack of orientation, but if the entrance is at B8, as you have just explained to me, then my room was on the left-hand side from the entrance, the second room. That is to say, the first room was the interrogation room, and I think my room was room B10, and the other women were in B11, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, I apologise for interrupting again. Witness J, do you see the building in front of you? Look in my direction, please. If you look at me, in my direction. Witness J, do you see the administration building on the model?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see the entrance on the model again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you move to the model that you have on the ELMO, where would you place the entrance? Where do you consider the entrance to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, the entrance is the hall which is marked B8; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Perhaps you could put your glasses on. The entrance, therefore, is B8. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the room that you spent time in was which one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was B10, as far as I can make out here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Okay. You mean where you're holding the pointer? Are you holding the pointer to at that place now? You've got the pointer and it's on B5. There is still this problem of translation, it appears, when they say "here" or "there," whereas the witness has changed positions. Now, let's have a definite answer. Which was your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was B10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] B10. Thank you. I apologise, Mr. Fila. You may continue now. The witness says B10.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in B11.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If you're tired, Witness, I don't want to tire you more and to tax you. And I keep looking at Mr. Keegan to see if it's all right, whether I can go on or not or whether I'm tiring you too much. So can I go on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, the Trial Chamber is here to guide you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, which room did you call the duty room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that according to this model, that room was B5.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now then, please tell us which room the incident with Krkan took place and the incident with the Captain took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In both cases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't require the model any more. You said that when you went to sleep -- the time that you went back to your room to sleep was usually after 7.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mostly. Half an hour -- give or take half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: As it was summertime, was it still daylight when you went back to your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you went back to your room at approximately 7.00 p.m., give or take half an hour, were the interrogations still ongoing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They had been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I am not -- I don't mean that somebody might have escaped, but I meant group interrogations, people would come in groups.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had been completed, because we couldn't enter the room otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. When you went into those rooms, into both those rooms, and when you cleared up so that you could sleep there, were you locked, closed in, locked in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean "closed in"?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Locked in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not locked in.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was there anybody standing outside the door, nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nearby, by the stairs on the left. There was always an armed guard there usually, although sometimes he wasn't there. But usually, in general, he was. In front of the reception room. There was always somebody standing on guard there. Usually, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You're talking about inside. I'm asking about outside.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the guard was outside in the corridor, to the left of the stairs. He was sitting on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you happen to know the name of that man or his nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst ourselves, we called him the "Machine-gunner," but I don't really know his real name and surname. We called him "Mitraljezac," "Machine-gunner." Now, whether that big gun was a machine-gun or not, but because of that gun we called him the "Machine-gunner."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where was the machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when he was on duty, he had that gun with him, that machine-gun, the man sitting down on the left-hand side of the stairway in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So this was a sort of mobile machine-gun, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could move it around.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was there a machine-gun outside on one of the roofs or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. Very often there would be a man on the roof with a weapon, but not all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm referring to the administration building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm referring to that building as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What I should like to know, at this point, is how able were you to move around during the night. Where were you allowed to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could go as far as the toilet and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you walk around the corridors? Could you go up to the roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could only go to the toilet. What do you mean to the roof? We didn't climb to the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes. But I mean if you were free enough to walk around, you could go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you want to say no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What do you mean by "free"? I wasn't free. I was detained. I could go to the toilet and back. That was the only trip I could take, except in cases when I was called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In your description of the two incidents that took place in the room that you indicated, something was left unclear to me. I'm not quite sure about the chronology. I don't know what happened first, the one involving Krkan or the one involving Captain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one involving Krkan took place first.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In response to a question put to you by Mr. Keegan, you said that it took place in the afternoon hours or sometime early in the evening.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So at that time, the visibility was still good.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was perhaps getting dark. It was summertime. I don't know what time it could have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about the time. It's not important. Do you know, by any chance, whether the interrogators were still there? Was there any light on there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interrogators were no longer there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What about the guards, other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know what shift was on duty at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume it was Krkan's shift. I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you please explain to me or, rather, tell me not the exact date but give me a time framework or a month when it took place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe it was in July or maybe in late June. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So after that incident, you spent a considerable amount of time in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And the incident did not reoccur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to that extent. Not the way it happened the first time. But there were other mistreatments, lesser mistreatments, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Well, regarding the thing that he said to you, that he would come one night with a mattress, do you agree with me that that never actually happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't do that, although --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you remember how he looked like during that period of time, how fat he was? You said he was quite fat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is it possible that he weighed over 125 kilos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I suppose that you weighed the same as you weigh today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Oh, no. I was much thinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thinner than now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, much thinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You said that you were both standing while this took place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That he pushed you against a wall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That he was touching you with both his hands.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So with one of his hands or both of his hands he took out his penis at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And you were facing each other all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And you claim that it is possible to have a sexual intercourse in that manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This concludes my cross-examination. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Fila. Mr. Stojanovic, your witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are ready to proceed with the cross-examination of the witness; however, I don't think that we would be able to complete it by the end of the working day today, as far as I'm informed. The Defence of Mr. Prcac also has quite a few questions for the witness. I don't know what is going to be the decision of the Chamber, but perhaps it would be more advisable to begin tomorrow and not to have to interrupt the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Masic, I don't know how much time you will need for the cross-examination because I should think so, that the counsel for Mr. Zigic has a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we will definitely need more than 20 minutes, so I don't think that I myself would be able to complete the cross-examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Masic. So in order not to be obliged to interrupt the cross-examination of the witness by the remaining Defence counsel and because we're not able to finish today, the idea was to complete the cross-examination of Witness J, but that seems to be impossible at this point, so I think we should continue with the remaining cross-examination tomorrow. Witness J, I'm afraid you'll have to come back tomorrow at half past nine because it looks like we're not able to complete your cross-examination today. I'm now going to ask the usher to lower down the blinds so that you can leave the courtroom with the full application of your protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: As I have promised to the Defence counsel of Mr. Prcac, I am now going to ask Madam Registrar to inform us about the results of their inquiry regarding the events that took place yesterday and this morning, apparently. Madam Registrar, could you please brief us and tell us if there is any news about the matter?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, President. The outcome of the investigation is that Mr. Prcac's prescription has been changed by his doctor since 1st of September, year 2000; therefore, the types and the numbers of tablets are changed accordingly which perhaps confused Mr. Prcac a little bit. The new prescription has been and is being and will always be strictly implemented. However, it is always our primary task to give full attention to the need of the accused. In the future, should any doubt about health issue arises again, we will always welcome the accused or his counsel to contact us, perhaps Mr. Mark Dubuisson, the chief of CNSS, and will guarantee a prompt and efficient response. And I hope this message satisfy the Defence and the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, Jovan Simic, does that message indeed satisfy you, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry, but I have to speak again, and I shall be very brief. We know about the change of the prescription, but in the conversation with the doctor it was agreed that the old prescription -- or rather, the old therapy would continue to be applied. As to the reasons of this new change, we don't know anything about it, but the medication was not given to Mr. Prcac on a regular basis. He was given medication today, and I hope that he will be given medication tonight as well. But what we insist upon is the regularity of the therapy, and we also want the old therapy to be applied. We do not know about the reasons for the change of therapy which followed later in time after our discussions with the doctor, and we don't know anything about it, and this is why we insist on the old therapy to be applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Simic, but please, bear in mind that if there is a problem, if there is a question to be raised, you should address Mr. Mark Dubuisson directly, and he will provide you with the answer. He's the one who knows whether he should take the old prescription or the new one. I'm not a physician; I cannot tell you that. You have to contact Mr. Mark Dubuisson if you have any problems of that kind, and I hope that there won't be any problems in the future. We're now going to adjourn for the day, but it seems that Mr. Keegan would like to speak. We understand also this non-verbal communication, but we would also like to hear him, Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Rather than raise matters in the morning, since we do have a little bit of time left, there are two matters, Your Honour, that I'd like to raise. One is that as we indicated at the end of last week, the Prosecution did develop a set of procedures for the remaining witnesses for in-court identification. We submitted those to the Defence. They've had time to consider them, and they are in agreement with these procedures, Your Honour. I have the copy here for the Judges to review. I apologise that the French version is not yet prepared. The procedure would be essentially the procedure I followed yesterday with Witness J, as you'll see. In particular, with respect to the issue of the accused having to remove headsets or to stand up, we would leave that to the witness, the witness being advised that if they feel it necessary or if they would so desire to have an individual stand up, then they may request that; otherwise, the accused may remain seated with their headphones on. The only thing that within this direction that we wouldn't advise the witness directly, but is, if you will -- we would submit an obligation or a requirement for the accused is that when we get to the part of an identification, that they would all at least look up and look at -- in the witness's direction so the witness can see their face just as they can see everyone else; and that with respect to Mr. Prcac, that he remove his eyeglasses. But outside of those, those issues, the rest of it would be, in essence, a question of whether the witness feels it's necessary to have someone stand or not. And if that would be acceptable to the Court, our proposal would be that the identification be led strictly by the Prosecution. The Defence, obviously, in cross-examination if they have additional questions with respect to the identification they want to raise, they are, of course, free to do that; but we would minimise the variations in the identification procedures so that all parties at least are -- would be confident in how the procedure would run in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, the Defence seems to agree with the proposed procedure. Can I hear the Defence, at least, for the record? Mr. Simic, Krstan Simic, according to the procedure that we have somehow established, is the spokesperson for the Defence, unless he himself gives the floor to anyone else. So Mr. Simic, would you please tell us what the position of the Defence is?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I shall be speaking on behalf of the Defence counsel of Mr. Kos, Radic, Prcac. We accept the proposed procedure, but I don't know what Mr. Stojanovic is going to say as far as the four of us are concerned. We are agreeable to the proposed procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovic, it seems that you do not agree with the procedure?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think it is a major disagreement. I have discussed the issue with my learned colleague Mr. Keegan. However, I have a problem with item G. The rest is beyond any dispute. However, we have proposed to Mr. Keegan either to delete this last particular item or to amend it slightly, and I have indicated to him in what way. So this last point, the last item, is slightly problematic for us because we view it as a kind of pressure exerted upon a witness. We can always ask a witness if there are any reasons for his not being sure about something, but we would even agree with the text as it is proposed with a small addition. It should be mentioned that the identification is fully completed with this last particular question, and it should also be stated -- it should also state any reasons for witnesses not being sure if such a case should occur. I also think that questions should be allowed after the identification process if things remain unclear. So I just wanted to state for the record that we would like a small amendment to be made in respect of the last item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I must confess that I apparently misunderstood my discussion with Mr. Stojanovic. This last section, G, of course, would only be applicable if the witness in making the identification then said something that made it clear that there may be a question about the identification. This G would not be read to the witness or otherwise addressed to the witness unless the witness somehow said, for example, "Well, I believe that's Mr. Prcac, but it's been nine years." Well, we would then ask him to explain that. Are you sure? Are you not sure? If you're not sure, why? That's when it would come up, because we have seen such identifications, and we think it's only fair that there be an explanation on the record for what that means. As we indicated previously, the Defence, of course, can always raise issues with respect to an identification during cross-examination. That's always the right of the Defence. So I thought I understood what Mr. Stojanovic was saying, and I understood that this in fact did address his concerns. But this is not something that would necessarily be raised in every case. It would only be raised if the witnesses themselves in the identification said something that indicated there may be some confusion, and rather than leave the record in that state, a follow-up question would be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it would be more advisable not to consider this document as a final document. Perhaps you can continue your discussion, and if you have anything else to add, please let us know. I think that we will call it a day at this point. There's nothing else that we can discuss.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: This second one will be brief, Your Honour, I promise. This last issue is the question of the time loss that we are incurring here in our procedures. We are, of course, extremely conscious of our time limit, but it also appears to the Prosecution that there are delays sometimes within the proceedings that are not directly attributable to the examination of the accused, and we have been attempting to record that. I only raise this because I would like to advise the Chamber that it is something that we're thinking about, and it may be an issue that we need to raise if it appears that we are going to be in trouble with respect to our deadline. I'm not certain at this point that we will be, so it may, in fact, not become an issue. But we did want to put it on the record that perhaps by the next session we'll have a better idea, meaning after we come back from the one-week break, of where we are and whether we may need to have a strict accounting for our time, if you will, because we believe that there may be some additional time that the Prosecution would merit if it is not going to be able to comply with the calendar date for that 21 days that we had left. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We are aware of that problem, Mr. Keegan; however, one should bear in mind the fact that very often we do lose time because the Prosecution hasn't organised itself properly. We shouldn't forget that. The Chamber would like to tell you, you and both parties, actually, that this is something we have to insist upon. Sometimes the Defence believes that they have to defend their client during the case for the Prosecution, so I have to say, once again, that the Defence will have their own time to lead their own evidence, and that they can conduct cross-examinations of their witnesses with that fact in mind. And the Prosecution will be in the same situation later on. We are not dealing only with character witnesses here. We have a number of fact witnesses, and I do think that we waste a lot of time discussing incidents which are not necessary. I think that we lose sometimes the procedure and the framework of the procedure from sight from time to time. I just wish to say that we do understand your position, and we are fully aware of the restrictions of time that have been imposed on the Prosecutor, and we know exactly what the reasons for various delays are. So to sum up and to finish this hearing, let me just remind Mr. Stojanovic of the time limits to file a request for leave to lodge an appeal because we should have in mind the possibility of us having to reorganise our time with the witnesses. We need to have as much information as possible, and we need to be briefed about the position of the parties regarding the appeal on time because we can organise accordingly. It is our task to see that justice is administered in a proper way, but we also have to be mindful of the time limits. We have five accused in this case, and each accused individually has a right to a speedy trial but also to a fair trial. This can also be put differently: Each of the accused has a right to a fair trial but also to a speedy trial. So bearing all that in mind, please do not forget the time limits regarding the appeal. This will help us a great deal when it comes to the organisation of our work. Thank you very much for your attention, and I think that we can wind up at this point. We will see each again tomorrow morning, half past nine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: be reconvened on Thursday the 7th day of September, 2000, at 9:30 a.m.
